enemies.grid_notes: BǪÐVARR BEAR-SARK (Rename Table, C-CLAN-LEAD-01), deck north half, elev 1. Fights by holmgang law: scripted alternating-strike opening rounds, then free AI within the circle. At the yield trigger he casts down his axe. He does not use full berserkergang — a point the scene makes: he is testing the boy, and some part of him is afraid of what full rage might meet (his dossier's 'will not switch off' seed).
Bjarnholt second, north bank at elev 2; intervenes ONLY if the law is broken (any non-duelist enters the circle, or the yield is violated).
Second lodge-brother, north bank beside e2; as e2.

The lodge's shield-bearer on the north shingle bar (elev 1), holding Bǫðvarr's three lawful replacement shields — the holmgang shield-count made visible; a mechanical pacing device (each 'shield break' = phase mark on e1's HP bar).

neutrals.grid_notes: Officiating goði (unnamed, minor — not Þorgeir) on the judge's stone slab at elev 3; reads the law at turn 1, calls the yield. Cannot be prevented from witnessing; leaves N when it ends.
Grím's second from the levy, south bank at elev 2 — his witness by right.
Shore-folk cluster on the south bank, elev 2 (abstracted as one unit); scatters if the law breaks.

objectives.primary: Win the holmgang: bring Bǫðvarr below 30% HP, or force him off the deck (knockback ring-out).
secondary: Never leave the law_circle yourself (leaving = forfeit, immediate defeat).
Win without spending a Wyrd Point — this duel is ALWAYS Sung, so any Wyrd use here is public and costs man_blood −4 (C-WYRD-02); winning clean is the deniability play (C-GRIM-05).
Win without Bǫðvarr's blood on the ice (pure ring-out) — the rarest, most-sung outcome.
objectives.defeat: Grím is downed or forced off the deck (seconds end it — defeat, not death; story battle).

triggers.note: The goði on the slab names the terms: to yield, to ring-out, or to three shields broken. Camera beat; establishes law_circle rules in UI.

Fires with law_is_read if the ford peddler's tale is loose: Bǫðvarr half-voices it before the first blow — 'they say the spears refuse you, smith's boy; let us see' — the suspicion that sharpened his blood-claim into a challenge.

He casts down his axe, names the wound-price paid, and offers his hand — a lawful yield before a full house. The accept/execute prompt writes the enum: 'honored' (take the hand: Sung mercy_terror +6, Bjarnholt seed planted) or 'executed' (kill a yielded man at a LAWFUL duel before witnesses: Sung mercy_terror −10, True −10, the guest-cup logic invoked — Bjarnholt enmity locked for Ch2, C-ALIGN-03/05: the game allows it and every hall will sing it). Ring-out (e1 pushed off the deck) resolves through this same yield beat — the law counts feet off lawful ground as the wound-price paid.
If Grím falls the seconds carry him off — defeat without permadeath; the challenge was to yield.

designer_notes.height_gimmick: The anti-elevation map: the deck is dead flat by LAW — sixteen plank tiles all at elevation 1, not one step of height to take — and the only meaningful edge is its rim, a 1h drop to the elevation-0 ice that means forfeit, not fall damage. Knockback becomes the whole vertical game: push the opponent's feet off the lawful ground and the duel is decided without a killing wound. Every other Ch1 map rewards taking height; this one forbids it, and makes facing and footwork carry everything (C-FACE-01 mastery test). The banks at elevation 2-3 exist only so the witnesses look DOWN into the fight like a bowl — height belongs to the audience here, never to the duelists.
designer_notes.witness_setup: There is no preventing testimony here and the design says so out loud: seconds on both banks (e2/e3 north, n2 south), an officiating goði on the elevation-3 judge's slab, shore-folk (n3) ringing the holm — a lawful duel EXISTS to be witnessed. witness_rule is always_sung (the sanctioned exception for scripted story beats): whatever happens on the deck enters the saga, including exactly how Bǫðvarr's yield is answered (holmgang_grith: honored | executed).
designer_notes.intent: Formal 1v1 with seconds standing off (ai script): facing mastery under holmgang law. Grím answers Bǫðvarr Bear-Sark's lawful challenge (blood-claim for a lodge kinsman fallen among the Landless at ch1-04, and half-voiced suspicion of the ford rumor). Duel is to yield, not death, per law (C-TONE-04): forcing Bǫðvarr below 30% or off the deck ends it. The grið answer afterward is the chapter's loudest mercy beat — performed for a full house.
